people.james-letter.role: Servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ
people.james-letter.relations: He writes to the twelve tribes in the Dispersion. He calls them brothers.
people.james-letter.meaning: James greets the twelve tribes in the Dispersion. He tells them to ask God for wisdom and to be doers of the word. He warns against favoring the rich and against careless speech. He tells the sick to call for the elders.
people.jesus.role: Lord Jesus Christ, our glorious Lord
people.jesus.relations: James calls himself a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ.
people.jesus.meaning: James names him in the greeting. James says not to hold the faith of our glorious Lord with partiality (chapter 2). A man in fine clothing gets a good seat. A poor man is told to stand. James calls that partiality.
people.abraham.role: Our father, called the friend of God
people.abraham.relations: James calls him our father. He ties his faith to his offering of Isaac.
people.abraham.meaning: James says Abraham offered up his son Isaac on the altar. Faith worked with his works. James quotes Scripture that Abraham believed God, and it was counted as righteousness. Abraham was called the friend of God.
people.isaac.role: Abraham’s son, offered on the altar
people.isaac.meaning: James names Isaac once. Abraham offered him up on the altar. James uses this act to show faith working with works.
people.rahab.role: Woman called a prostitute, who received the messengers
people.rahab.relations: James places her after Abraham as a second example.
people.rahab.meaning: James calls her Rahab the prostitute. She received the messengers and sent them out another way. James says she was justified by works, as Abraham was.
people.job.relations: James says his readers have heard of his perseverance. They have seen the Lord in the outcome.
people.job.meaning: James tells the readers to be patient until the coming of the Lord. He calls those who endured blessed. He names Job’s perseverance. He says the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
people.elijah.role: Prophet whose prayer stopped and brought rain
people.elijah.relations: James says he was a man with a nature like ours.
people.elijah.meaning: James says Elijah prayed earnestly that it might not rain. It did not rain for three years and six months. He prayed again, and the sky gave rain. James uses him to show that a righteous person’s prayer is powerful.
sources.web.summary: The full text of James is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: James is the named speaker. Which James he is was not checked independently. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, and manuscripts were not checked either. The addressed communities and any full match with other letters were not checked. The unnamed trading city in chapter 4 has no known location.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-47.summary: The lesson joins seeking wisdom, patient endurance, active faith, and careful words.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-47.limits: For James, the lesson covers chapters 1, 2, 3, and 5. Its use of Joseph Smith’s experience is Church teaching. Linked Restoration passages, a talk, and a video were not reviewed independently.
sources.sigmon-james.summary: Sigmon links favoring the wealthy to a gap between professed faith and conduct.
sources.sigmon-james.limits: This is Sigmon’s own reading. Her wide claims about money and her use of ancient writings were not checked independently. Her modern political claims and linked campaign material were not checked either.
chapters.*.mapNote: James names no place, so the map shows none. The city in chapter 4 is unnamed.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: James names no travel route, so the map draws none.
